messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• In cities: 25–35 mph.
• Rural roads: 55 mph unless posted otherwise. | Speed limits can be lower in construction zones or school zones. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑seat or booster.
• Children under 4 must be in a rear‑seat child‑seat. | Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations carry a $50 fine. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• For commercial drivers, the limit is 0.04 %.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas has a “zero‑tolerance” law for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %). | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks.
• Stop signs require a full stop before proceeding. | Failure to yield can lead to traffic citations. | | **School‑Zone Speed Limits** | • 20 mph during school hours (usually 7 a.m.–9 p.m.).
• 25 mph during other times. | Speeding in school zones can result in a $100 fine. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Passing on the right is prohibited unless the left lane is occupied. | Improper lane changes can lead to citations. | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, or when visibility is reduced.
• Fog lights are allowed only in fog or heavy rain. | Failure to use headlights can result in a $50 fine. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display valid registration stickers.
• Towing a vehicle requires a valid license and insurance. | Unregistered vehicles can be towed and fined. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces (unless you have a permit), or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a “no parking” zone can result in a $50 fine. | Violations may also lead to towing. | | **Traffic Camera Enforcement** | • Cameras enforce speed limits, red‑light violations, and other infractions. | Fines are issued by mail; you can contest them in court. | | **Traffic Court** | • Most traffic tickets are processed in local courts.
• You can pay online, appear in person, or contest the ticket. | Ignoring a ticket can lead to a warrant and higher fines. | ### How to Find Specific Laws - **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary source for all traffic laws. - **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – Offers guides, FAQs, and downloadable handbooks. - **Local County Courts** – Provide information on how to handle tickets and traffic violations. ### Quick Tips 1. **Always obey posted signs** – they override general rules. 2. **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on the phone. 3. **Check your local county’s website** for specific ordinances (e.g., parking restrictions). 4. **If you receive a ticket**, decide early whether to pay, contest, or attend a traffic school (if eligible). Feel free to ask if you need details on a particular rule or how to handle a specific ticket!
